The Wealth of Nations, Adam Smith, edited by Edwin Cannan.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/adam-smith/the-wealth-of-nations

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Adam Smith, the author, died 1790.
- Edwin Cannan, the editor (introduction and notes), died 1935.

First publication of the text used: 1776 (SE colophon: 'The Wealth of Nations was published in 1776 by Adam Smith.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1776, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (Great Britain (first published in London, 9 March 1776, by W. Strahan and T. Cadell; Wikipedia infobox 'The Wealth of Nations': country Scotland, Kingdom of Great Britain)): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1935, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2006.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
